title: The Falling Calendar
text: Made it to Starfall Trench!~ The stars really do fall all the way down here. Apparently travelers used to tell the seasons by their colors. Blue-white meant safe passage. Glimmer insists the bright pink ones mean 'snack time.' I am fairly certain Glimmer made that up.

title: Stone That Remembers Heat
text: Fresh starstone stays warm long after it falls. I found one buried deep in an old crater and it started glowing brighter when I carried it closer to the center. Naturally I spent twenty minutes moving it back and forth. For research. Definitely not because the shiny rock was entertaining.

title: Gravity Has Opinions
text: My compass works. My map works. Gravity does NOT work. I dropped a pebble and it fell sideways. Then another fell behind me. Glimmer has been floating upside down for ten minutes and seems extremely pleased with this development.

title: Crystalline Nursery
text: Tiny glass-finned fish live inside the meteor cracks! Whenever something larger swims nearby, the crystal walls start ringing and scare it away. I tried tapping one gently. The entire nursery rang back. I apologized. The fish did not accept my apology.

title: Do Not Lick the Comet
text: Important scientific discovery: cometglass tastes like cold lightning. Secondary scientific discovery: I should stop testing whether strange glowing objects taste like anything. Glimmer watched me do it and somehow looked disappointed without having a face.

title: A Familiar Mark
text: I found an old cargo seal buried beneath the trench today. The workmanship looks almost exactly like the Moonlit Lab ruins... but this one says Starfall Annex. Different place. Same symbols. Much newer markings, too. I don't like that part. Naturally, I am going to investigate it.

title: The Quiet Impact
text: Found a crater where absolutely nothing makes noise. No current. No bubbles. Even my footsteps disappear at the edge. Glimmer chimed before entering and the sound just... stopped. We left pretty quickly. I wrote 'NOPE' on a nearby stone for the next explorer.

title: Ventkeeper Tricks
text: The cosmic vents turn iron ridiculously heavy, but copper works normally. I learned this after trying to lift my gear beside one and nearly becoming part of the floor. Somewhere, an ancient Ventkeeper is probably laughing at me.

title: Stars From Somewhere Else
text: The fallen fragments down here form constellations I can't find anywhere in the sky. I checked twice. Then three times. Either my astronomy is terrible—which is completely possible—or some of these stars fell from somewhere we can't see.

title: Helpful Arrow Number Seven
text: I found seven tunnels and drew an arrow toward the shortcut. Then I realized another tunnel might be faster, so I drew another arrow. Then another. There are now seven arrows. Glimmer has refused to follow any of them. Honestly? Fair.

title: The Starcoil Shell
text: I found a beautiful nautilus shell with a spiral that matches an orbit on an old star chart. Problem: that star isn't on any modern chart I own. I showed Glimmer. Glimmer chimed once and hid in my hood. Very informative, thank you.

title: A Ruin That Knew
text: There's an old arch here that predates the crater around it, but its carvings show the star falling anyway. I stared at it for a long time trying to understand how someone carved an event before it happened. My conclusion: Starfall Trench is cheating.

title: The Trench Sings
text: Several meteor shards started humming together today. At first I thought something enormous was approaching and very bravely hid behind a rock. Turns out they were playing an old navigation melody! I tried humming along. The shards stopped. Rude.

title: Ceiling: 3, Shizuki: 0
text: I woke up on the ceiling again. THIRD TIME. I am tying my bedroll to the floor tonight. Glimmer, who does not need a bedroll and can float whenever it wants, has been absolutely unbearable about this.

title: Emergency Mustache Protocol
text: Found an old security notice near the Annex. It says disguises are ineffective against automated constructs. I added a fake mustache to the diagram anyway. Scientific conclusion: ineffective against security constructs. Extremely effective for morale.

title: A Hundred Years Ago
text: I uncovered a cracked observation lens that doesn't magnify distance—it shows places as they looked long ago. I pointed it toward the ruins and, for a moment, everything was standing again. Lights. Doors. People moving inside. Then the lens cracked a little more and the image vanished. I think I'm keeping my hands off this one.

title: Something Ate the Stars
text: There are smooth trails carved through the stone ending at empty places where star fragments should be. Whatever removed them left silver residue behind. Glimmer wants to follow the trail. I would like to formally record that for once, I am the responsible one.

title: Absolutely Normal Cargo
text: Found part of an old Annex shipping complaint. Whoever wrote it was VERY upset about receiving sealed crates with no origin labels and no warning about whether the contents were alive. Which means someone, somewhere, apparently had to write: 'Please tell us if the box is alive.' I almost respect the chaos.

title: Aurora From Below
text: An aurora rose out of the seafloor tonight. Not from the sky—the ground. It turned the whole trench blue and violet, then reversed the current and sent half my supplies floating past my head. Beautiful! Majestic! I would like my other boot back.

title: Something Underneath
text: I found an old badge near the Annex. It has the same organization mark I've seen before, but there's another symbol underneath it that someone deliberately scratched away. I tried holding it toward the light. Glimmer immediately knocked it out of my hand. I'm beginning to think the sprite has better survival instincts than I do.

title: Cometglass Etiquette
text: Old travelers apparently believed taking the first cometglass shard from a fresh crater made the falling stars 'notice' you. Obviously superstition. Completely ridiculous. Anyway, I waited until the SECOND shard before taking one. There's no reason to be reckless.

title: The Weightless Camp
text: Found an old campsite built around a floating boulder. Every bedroll was tied down. Every storage box was tied down. Even the cooking pot was tied down. Whoever camped here understood Starfall much better than I did on night one. I am stealing this strategy immediately.

title: They Kept Searching
text: The deeper Annex records keep mentioning upgraded pursuit systems—revision after revision, long after the Moonlit Lab should have been abandoned. They were still looking for something. Or someone. I have a very uncomfortable guess about who.

title: The Fallen Star Walker
text: There are footprints fused into the stone here, but they don't begin anywhere and they don't end anywhere. Just a line of glowing steps across the crater. I put one foot beside them for comparison. Much bigger than mine. Glimmer has voted that we do NOT follow them. Motion carried unanimously.

title: Return Visit
text: Found another Annex room today. I moved one chair exactly three feet to the left and wrote: 'I came back voluntarily, moved your furniture, and left voluntarily. Important distinction.' Petty? Maybe. Satisfying? Absolutely.

title: The Bigger Map
text: I finally found a damaged celestial chart inside the Annex. Moonlit Lab and Starfall aren't the only marked locations. There were other points farther out, but the names are ruined. One path seems to continue toward a forest wrapped in glowing currents. I knew the Astral Sea was big, but... maybe I didn't know how big.

title: The Corekeeper
text: A maintenance record describes an artificial guardian built to keep functioning long after the people who made it were gone. That's unsettling enough on its own. Then I found fresh-looking scratches near the old chamber door. I have decided this is a problem for Future Shizuki.

title: Subject Seven
text: I found those words again today. 'Subject Seven transfer materials.' The destination was cut out of the record. Seeing that number still makes my stomach twist, even after all this time. Glimmer stayed unusually quiet. I folded the page and kept moving. I'm not letting an old number decide where I go next.

title: Annex Night Watch
text: Found an old guard log complaining about laughter in sealed ducts and someone putting paper mustaches on every Officer portrait. I would like it officially recorded that this happened LONG before I got here. I am innocent. Completely innocent. ...I did fix one of the mustaches, though. It was crooked.

title: The Trench Wasn't the End
text: The last intact Annex ledger confirms it: Moonlit Lab and Starfall Annex answered to the same organization, and neither one was operating alone. There are more marks on the old maps—more places, more paths, more questions. One route disappears into a forest where travelers wrote that the currents themselves whisper back. Glimmer is already heading that way. I suppose that's my answer, then~
